readings.title: The Barber's Razor and the Divided Hair
readings.subtitle: A Prophetic Sign of Jerusalem's Threefold Destruction
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 5:1] “And you, son of man, take a sharp sword, take it as a barber’s razor, and you shall pass it over your head and your beard. And you shall take scales to weigh and divide <dn>את</dn> the hair.
[2] “Burn with fire one-third in the midst of the city when the days of the siege are completed. And you shall take one-third and strike around it with the sword, and scatter one-third in the wind. And <dn>I</dn> shall draw out a sword after them.
[3] “And you shall take a few hairs from there and bind them in the edge of your garment.
[4] “And take again some of them, and throw them into the midst of the fire, and burn them in the fire. From it a fire shall spread unto all the house of Yisra’ěl.
[5] “Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘This is Yerushalayim which <dn>I</dn> have set in the midst of the nations, with the other lands all around her.</dq>
[6] <dq>But she rebelled against <dn>My</dn> rightrulings, doing wrong, more than the nations, and <dn>My</dn> laws more than the lands all around her. For they have rejected <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, and they have not walked in <dn>My</dn> laws.’</dq>
[7] “Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Because you have rebelled more than the nations all around you, and have not walked in <dn>My</dn> laws, nor done <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, nor even done according to the right-rulings of the nations all around you,’</dq>
[8] <dq>therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘Look <dn>I</dn> <dn>My</dn>self am against you and shall execute <dn>את</dn> judgments in your midst before the eyes of the nations.</dq>
[9] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall do among you what <dn>I</dn> have never done, and the like of which <dn>I</dn> never do again, because of all your abominations.</dq>
[10] <dq>Therefore fathers are going to eat <dn>את</dn> their sons in your midst, and sons eat <dn>את</dn> their fathers. And <dn>I</dn> shall execute <dn>את</dn> judgments among you and scatter <dn>את</dn> all your remnant to all the winds.</dq>
[11] <dq>Therefore, as <dn>I</dn> live,’</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘because you have defiled <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> set-apart place with all your disgusting matters and with all your abominations, therefore <dn>I</dn> also withdraw. And <dn>My</dn> eye shall not pardon, nor shall <dn>I</dn> spare.</dq>
[12] <dq>One-third of you shall die of pestilence, and be consumed with scarcity of food in your midst. And one-third shall fall by the sword all around you. And <dn>I</dn> shall scatter another third to all the winds, and draw out a sword after them.</dq>
[13] <dq>And <dn>My</dn> displeasure shall be completed. And <dn>I</dn> shall bring <dn>My</dn> wrath to rest upon them, and <dn>I</dn> shall be eased. And they shall know that <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have spoken it in <dn>My</dn> ardour, when <dn>I</dn> have completed <dn>My</dn> wrath upon them.</dq>
[14] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall make you a waste and a reproach among the nations that are all around you, before the eyes of all who pass by.</dq>
[15] <dq>And it shall be a reproach, an object of scorn, a warning, and an astonishment to the nations that are all around you, when <dn>I</dn> execute <dn>את</dn> judgments among you in displeasure and in wrath and in heated chastisements. <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have spoken.</dq>
[16] <dq>When <dn>I</dn> send against them <dn>את</dn> the evil arrows of scarcity of food which shall be for their destruction, which <dn>I</dn> send to destroy you, <dn>I</dn> shall increase the scarcity of food upon you and cut off your supply of bread.</dq>
[17] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall send against you scarcity of food and evil beasts, and they shall bereave you. And pestilence and blood shall pass through you, while <dn>I</dn> bring the sword against you. <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have spoken.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Prophecy Against the Mountains of Israel
readings.subtitle: The Destruction of Idolatrous High Places and the Promise of a Remnant
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 6:1] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying,
[2] “Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Yisra’ěl, and prophesy against them.
[3] “And you shall say, <dq>‘O mountains of Yisra’ěl, hear <dn>את</dn> the word of the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!’ Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to the mountains, to the hills, to the ravines, and to the valleys, “Look, <dn>I</dn> <dn>My</dn>self am bringing a sword against you, and <dn>I</dn> shall destroy <dn>את</dn> your high places.</dq>
[4] <dq>“And your slaughter-places shall be ruined, your sun-pillars shall be broken in pieces. And <dn>I</dn> shall make your slain fall in front of your idols,</dq>
[5] <dq>and lay <dn>את</dn> the corpses of the children of Yisra’ěl in front of their idols, and scatter <dn>את</dn> your bones all around your slaughter-places.</dq>
[6] <dq>“In all your dwelling places the cities shall be destroyed and the high places deserted, so that your slaughter-places are broken and bear their punishment. And your idols shall be smashed and made to cease, and your sun-pillars cut down, and your works blotted out.</dq>
[7] <dq>“And the slain shall fall in your midst, and you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[8] <dq>“But <dn>I</dn> shall leave a remnant, in that some of you shall escape the sword among the nations, when you are scattered throughout the lands.</dq>
[9] <dq>“And those of you who escape shall remember <dn>את</dn> <dn>Me</dn> among the nations where they have been taken captive, because <dn>I</dn> have been broken by their adulterous heart which has turned away from <dn>Me</dn>, and by their eyes which whored after their idols. And they shall loathe themselves for the evils which they have done in all their abominations.</dq>
[10] <dq>“And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and not for naught have <dn>I</dn> spoken to do this evil to them.”</dq>
[11] Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Strike with your hand and stamp your feet, and say, ‘Alas, because of all the evil abominations of the house of Yisra’ěl who shall fall by sword, by scarcity of food, and by pestilence!</dq>
[12] <dq>He who is far off shall die by pestilence, he who is near fall by the sword, and he who is left over and is besieged die by scarcity of food. And <dn>I</dn> shall complete <dn>My</dn> wrath upon them.</dq>
[13] <dq>And you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, when their slain are among their idols all around their slaughter-places, on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, under every green tree, and under every thick oak, wherever they offered sweet incense to all their idols.</dq>
[14] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall stretch out <dn>My</dn> hand against them and make <dn>את</dn> the land a wasteland, even more waste than the wilderness toward Diḇlah, in all their dwelling places. And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ” ’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The End Has Come
readings.subtitle: Judgment on the Four Corners of the Land
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 7:1] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying,
[2] “And you, son of man, this is what the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to the land of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘An end! The end has come upon the four corners of the land.</dq>
[3] <dq>Now the end is upon you, and <dn>I</dn> shall send <dn>My</dn> displeasure against you, and judge you according to your ways, and repay you for all your abominations.</dq>
[4] <dq>And <dn>My</dn> eye shall not pardon you, nor would <dn>I</dn> spare, for <dn>I</dn> repay your ways while your abominations are in your midst. And you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!’</dq>
[5] “Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘A calamity, an only calamity, look, it has come!</dq>
[6] <dq>An end has come, the end has come! It has awakened against you, look, it has come!</dq>
[7] <dq>The turn has come to you, O inhabitants of the land. The time has come, a day of uproar is near, and not of rejoicing in the mountains.</dq>
[8] <dq>Soon <dn>I</dn> shall pour out <dn>My</dn> wrath, and shall complete <dn>My</dn> displeasure upon you, and judge you according to your ways, and repay you for all your abominations.</dq>
[9] <dq>And <dn>My</dn> eye shall not pardon, nor would <dn>I</dn> spare. <dn>I</dn> give you according to your ways while your abominations are in your midst. And you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who strikes.</dq>
[10] <dq>See, the day! See, it has come! The turn has come, the rod has blossomed, pride has budded.</dq>
[11] <dq>The violence has grown into a rod of wrongdoing. There is none of them, and none of its crowd, and none of their riches, and none eminent among them.</dq>
[12] <dq>The time has come, and the day has arrived. ‘Let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn, for wrath is on all its crowd.</dq>
[13] <dq>For the seller shall not return to what has been sold, though they are still alive. For the vision is for all its crowd – it shall not turn back. And in the crookedness of his life a man shall not strengthen himself.</dq>

readings.title: The Day of Wrath
readings.subtitle: The Collapse of Society and the Profaning of the Temple
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 7:14] <dq>They have blown the trumpet and all is prepared, but no one goes to battle, for <dn>My</dn> wrath is on all its crowd.</dq>
[15] <dq>The sword is outside, and the pestilence and the scarcity of food inside. He who is in the field dies by the sword, and he who is in a city, scarcity of food and pestilence devour him,</dq>
[16] <dq>while they who escape of them shall escape and be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them mourning, each for his crookedness.</dq>
[17] <dq>All hands go limp, and all knees become as water.</dq>
[18] <dq>And they shall gird on sackcloth, and be covered with trembling. And shame shall be on every face, and baldness on all their heads.</dq>
[19] <dq>They throw their silver into the streets, and their gold becomes as filth. Their silver and their gold is unable to deliver them in the day of the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. They do not satisfy their appetite, nor fill their stomachs, because it has been their stumbling-block of crookedness.</dq>
[20] <dq>And the splendour of <dn>His</dn> ornaments, <dn>He</dn> set it in excellency. But they made from it <dn>את</dn> the images of their abominations and their disgusting matters. Therefore <dn>I</dn> shall make it like filth to them.</dq>
[21] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall give it for a prey into the hands of strangers, and to the wrong of the earth for a spoil, and they shall profane it.</dq>
[22] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall turn <dn>My</dn> face from them. And they shall profane <dn>My</dn> secret place, for destroyers shall enter it and profane it.</dq>
[23] <dq>Make a chain, for the land has been filled with crimes of blood, and the city has been filled with violence.</dq>
[24] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall bring the evil ones of the nations, and they shall possess their houses. And <dn>I</dn> shall cause the pride of the strong to cease, and their set-apart places shall be profaned.</dq>
[25] <dq>Destruction shall come. And they shall seek peace, but there is none.</dq>
[26] <dq>Calamity upon calamity shall come, and report shall be upon report. And they shall seek a vision from a prophet. But the teaching has perished from the priest, and counsel from the elders!</dq>
[27] <dq>Let the sovereign mourn, and let the prince put on despair, and let the hands of the common people tremble. And <dn>I</dn> shall deal with them according to their way, and judge them with their own right-rulings. And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Abominations in the Temple
readings.subtitle: A Vision of Idolatry in the House of YeHoVaH
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 8:1] And it came to be in the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth of the new moon, as I sat in my house with the elders of Yehuḏah sitting before me, that the hand of the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> fell upon me there.
[2] And I looked and saw a likeness, like the appearance of fire. From <dn>His</dn> waist and downward the appearance was like fire, and from <dn>His</dn> waist and upward the appearance of brightness, like glowing metal.
[3] And <dn>He</dn> stretched out the form of a hand, and took me by a lock of my hair. And the Spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heavens, and brought me in visions of <dn>Elohim</dn> to Yerushalayim, to the door of the north gate of the inner court, where the seat of the image of jealousy was, which causes jealousy.
[4] And see, the esteem of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl was there, like the vision that I saw in the plain.
[5] And <dn>He</dn> said to me, <dq>“Son of man, please lift your eyes toward the north.”</dq> And I lifted my eyes northward, and north of the slaughter-place gate I saw this image of jealousy in the entrance.
[6] And <dn>He</dn> said to me, <dq>“Son of man, do you see what they are doing, the great abominations which the house of Yisra’ěl are doing here, driving <dn>Me</dn> away from <dn>My</dn> set-apart place? And you are to see still greater abominations.”</dq>
[7] Then <dn>He</dn> brought me to the door of the court. And I looked and saw a hole in the wall.
[8] And <dn>He</dn> said to me, <dq>“Son of man, please dig into the wall.”</dq> And when I dug into the wall I saw a door.
[9] And <dn>He</dn> said to me, <dq>“Go in, and see <dn>את</dn> the evil abominations which they are doing there.”</dq>
[10] And I went in and looked and saw all kinds of creeping creatures, abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Yisra’ěl, carved all around on the walls.
[11] And facing them stood seventy men of the elders of the house of Yisra’ěl, and in their midst stood Ya‛azanyahu son of Shaphan. Each one had a censer in his hand, and a thick cloud of incense went up.
[12] And <dn>He</dn> said to me, <dq>“Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Yisra’ěl are doing in the dark, each one in the room of his idols? For they say, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does not see us, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has forsaken the land.’ ”</dq>
[13] And <dn>He</dn> said to me, <dq>“You are to see still greater abominations which they are doing.”</dq>
[14] And <dn>He</dn> brought me to the door of the north gate of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and I saw women sitting there, weeping for Tammuz.
[15] Then <dn>He</dn> said to me, <dq>“Have you seen this, O son of man? You are to see still greater abominations than these.”</dq>
[16] And <dn>He</dn> brought me into the inner court of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And there, at the door of the Hěḵal of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, between the porch and the slaughter-place, were about twenty-five men with their backs toward the Hěḵal of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and their faces toward the east, and they were bowing themselves eastward to the sun.
[17] And <dn>He</dn> said to me, <dq>“Have you seen, O son of man? Is it a small matter to the house of Yehuḏah to do <dn>את</dn> the abominations which they have done here? For they have filled <dn>את</dn> the land with violence, and turn back to provoke <dn>Me</dn>. And see, they are putting the branch to <dn>My</dn> nose.</dq>
[18] <dq>“Therefore <dn>I</dn> shall indeed deal in wrath. <dn>My</dn> eye shall not pardon nor would <dn>I</dn> spare. And they shall cry in <dn>My</dn> ears with a loud voice, but <dn>I</dn> shall not hear them.”</dq>

readings.title: Judgment Begins at the Sanctuary
readings.subtitle: The Marking of the Faithful and the Slaying of the Wicked
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 9:1] And <dn>He</dn> called out in my hearing with a loud voice, saying, <dq>“Let the punishers of the city draw near, each with his weapon of destruction in his hand.”</dq>
[2] And look, six men came from the direction of the upper gate, which faces north, each with his battle-axe in his hand. And one man in their midst was clothed with linen and had a writer’s ink-horn at his side. And they came in and stood beside the bronze slaughter-place.
[3] And the esteem of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl went up from the keruḇ, where it had been, to the threshold of the House. And <dn>He</dn> called to the man clothed with linen, who had the writer’s ink-horn at his side,
[4] and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Pass on into the midst of the city, into the midst of Yerushalayim, and you shall put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and cry over all the abominations that are done within it.”</dq>
[5] And to the others <dn>He</dn> said in my hearing, <dq>“Pass on into the city after him and strike, do not let your eye pardon nor spare.</dq>
[6] <dq>“Kill to destruction old, young men, maidens and children and women, but do not come near anyone upon whom is the mark, and begin at <dn>My</dn> set-apart place.”</dq> So they began with the elders who were in front of the House.
[7] And <dn>He</dn> said to them, <dq>“Defile <dn>את</dn> the House, and fill <dn>את</dn> the courts with the slain. Go out!”</dq> And they went out and struck in the city.
[8] And as they were striking them it came to be that I alone was left. And I fell on my face and cried out, and said, “Ah, Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! Are You destroying all the remnant of Yisra’ěl in pouring out Your wrath on Yerushalayim?”
[9] And <dn>He</dn> said to me, <dq>“The crookedness of the house of Yisra’ěl and Yehuḏah is exceedingly great, and the land is filled with bloodshed, and the city filled with that which is warped. For they say, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has forsaken the land, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is not seeing!’</dq>
[10] <dq>“But as for <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>My</dn> eye shall not pardon, nor would <dn>I</dn> spare, <dn>I</dn> shall recompense their deeds on their own head.”</dq>
[11] And see, the man clothed with linen, who had the ink-horn at his side, reported back and said, “I have done as You commanded me.”
